title: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics · Practice paper 1
subject: Mathematics
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 38 questions. All questions are compulsory.
This question paper is divided into five Sections - A, B, C, D and E.
In Section A, Questions no. 1 to 18 are multiple choice questions (MCQs) and Questions no. 19 and 20 are Assertion-Reason based questions of 1 mark each.
In Section B, Questions no. 21 to 25 are Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions, carrying 2 marks each.
In Section C, Questions no. 26 to 31 are Short Answer (SA) type questions, carrying 3 marks each.
In Section D, Questions no. 32 to 35 are Long Answer (LA) type questions, carrying 5 marks each.

In Section E, Questions no. 36 to 38 are case study based questions carrying 4 marks each. The first two case study questions have three sub-parts (i), (ii), (iii) of 1, 1 and 2 marks; the third has two sub-parts of 2 marks each.
Internal choices of the board paper are not included: each question has one version.
Draw neat and clean figures wherever required. Take π = 22/7 wherever required, if not stated.
Use of calculators is not allowed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The value of $\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) - \sec^{-1}(-2)$ is
questions.sol: $\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}=\frac{\pi}{3}$. The principal value branch of $\sec^{-1}$ is $[0,\pi]-\{\frac{\pi}{2}\}$, so $\sec^{-1}(-2)=\frac{2\pi}{3}$. Value $=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\frac{\pi}{3}$.

questions.sol: $-1\le 3x-2\le 1 \Rightarrow 1\le 3x\le 3 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{3}\le x\le 1$.

questions.text: If $\cos^{-1}x=\frac{2\pi}{3}$, then the value of $\sin^{-1}x$ is
questions.sol: $x=\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\frac{1}{2}$. The principal value of $\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)$ lies in $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ and equals $-\frac{\pi}{6}$.

questions.text: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & a & 3\\ -2 & 0 & b\\ c & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$ is a skew-symmetric matrix, then the value of $a+b+c$ is
questions.sol: For a skew-symmetric matrix $a_{ij}=-a_{ji}$: $a=-(-2)=2$, $b=-1$, $c=-3$. So $a+b+c=2-1-3=-2$.

questions.sol: For a matrix $B$ of order 3, $|\operatorname{adj}B|=|B|^{2}$. Here $|2A|=2^{3}|A|=40$, so $|\operatorname{adj}(2A)|=40^{2}=1600$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The derivative of $\log(\sec x+\tan x)$ with respect to $x$ is
questions.sol: $\frac{d}{dx}\log(\sec x+\tan x)=\frac{\sec x\tan x+\sec^{2}x}{\sec x+\tan x}=\frac{\sec x(\tan x+\sec x)}{\sec x+\tan x}=\sec x$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}kx^{2}+2, & x\le 2\\ 3x-2, & x\gt 2\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=2$, then the value of $k$ is
questions.sol: Continuity at $x=2$: $f(2)=4k+2$ and $\lim_{x\to 2^{+}}(3x-2)=4$. So $4k+2=4 \Rightarrow k=\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The function $f(x)=x^{3}-6x^{2}+9x+5$ is strictly decreasing in the interval
questions.sol: $f'(x)=3x^{2}-12x+9=3(x-1)(x-3)$, which is negative only for $1\lt x\lt 3$.

questions.text: The rate of change of the volume of a sphere with respect to its radius $r$, when $r=3$ cm, is
questions.sol: $V=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} \Rightarrow \frac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^{2}=4\pi(9)=36\pi\ \mathrm{cm^{3}/cm}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The order and degree of the differential equation $\left(\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right)^{3}+\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^{4}+y=0$ are respectively
questions.sol: The highest order derivative is $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$, so the order is 2. The equation is a polynomial in the derivatives and the highest power of $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$ is 3, so the degree is 3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: $\int e^{x}(\sin x+\cos x)\,dx$ is equal to
questions.sol: Using $\int e^{x}\{f(x)+f'(x)\}dx=e^{x}f(x)+C$ with $f(x)=\sin x$, $f'(x)=\cos x$, the integral is $e^{x}\sin x+C$.

questions.sol: $\cos\theta=\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A die is thrown twice. The probability that the sum of the numbers is 8, given that the first throw shows an even number, is
questions.sol: First throw even: 18 outcomes. Of these, sum 8 occurs for $(2,6),(4,4),(6,2)$: 3 outcomes. Probability $=\frac{3}{18}=\frac{1}{6}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: $A$ and $B$ are independent events with $P(A)=\frac{1}{3}$ and $P(B)=\frac{1}{4}$. The probability that neither $A$ nor $B$ occurs is
questions.sol: $P(A'\cap B')=P(A')P(B')=\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{3}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): $\int_{-1}^{1}x|x|\,dx=0$.
Reason (R): $f(x)=x|x|$ is an even function.
Select the correct option.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: $f(-x)=(-x)|-x|=-x|x|=-f(x)$, so $x|x|$ is an odd function and its integral over $[-1,1]$ is 0. The Assertion is true; the Reason is false.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{2xy}$ is a homogeneous differential equation.
Reason (R): $F(x,y)=\frac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{2xy}$ satisfies $F(\lambda x,\lambda y)=\lambda^{0}F(x,y)$ for every non-zero $\lambda$.
Select the correct option.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: $F(\lambda x,\lambda y)=\frac{\lambda^{2}(x^{2}+y^{2})}{\lambda^{2}\cdot 2xy}=F(x,y)$, so $F$ is homogeneous of degree zero, which is exactly why the equation is homogeneous. Both are true and R explains A.

$3(2)+k(4)+(-2)(5)=0 \Rightarrow 4k-4=0 \Rightarrow k=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The corner points of the bounded feasible region of a linear programming problem are $(0,0)$, $(5,0)$, $(4,3)$ and $(0,6)$. The objective function is $Z=px+qy$, where $p, q\gt 0$. Find the relation between $p$ and $q$ so that the maximum value of $Z$ occurs at both the points $(5,0)$ and $(4,3)$.
questions.model:
Since the maximum occurs at both $(5,0)$ and $(4,3)$, $Z(5,0)=Z(4,3)$.
$5p=4p+3q \Rightarrow p=3q$
(Check: with $p=3q$, $Z(5,0)=Z(4,3)=15q$, which is more than $Z(0,6)=6q$ and $Z(0,0)=0$.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A water tank is in the shape of an inverted right circular cone of height 9 m and radius of the top 3 m, with its axis vertical. Water is pumped into the tank at the constant rate of $2\pi\ \mathrm{m^{3}}$ per minute. Find the rate at which the water level is rising when the depth of water in the tank is 6 m.
questions.model:
Let $h$ be the depth and $r$ the radius of the water surface at time $t$. By similar triangles, $\frac{r}{h}=\frac{3}{9} \Rightarrow r=\frac{h}{3}$.
$V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h=\frac{1}{3}\pi\frac{h^{2}}{9}h=\frac{\pi h^{3}}{27}$
$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{\pi h^{2}}{9}\frac{dh}{dt}$
At $h=6$: $2\pi=\frac{\pi(36)}{9}\frac{dh}{dt}=4\pi\frac{dh}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{1}{2}$
The water level is rising at $\frac{1}{2}$ m/min (0.5 m per minute).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{x}=x^{2}$, $x\gt 0$, given that $y=1$ when $x=1$.
questions.model:
This is linear with $P=\frac{1}{x}$, $Q=x^{2}$.
I.F. $=e^{\int\frac{1}{x}dx}=e^{\log x}=x$
Solution: $xy=\int x\cdot x^{2}\,dx=\frac{x^{4}}{4}+C$
$y(1)=1$: $1=\frac{1}{4}+C \Rightarrow C=\frac{3}{4}$
Particular solution: $xy=\frac{x^{4}}{4}+\frac{3}{4}$, i.e. $y=\frac{x^{3}}{4}+\frac{3}{4x}$

questions.text:
Solve the following linear programming problem graphically:
Maximise $Z=2x+5y$
subject to the constraints $x+y\le 9$, $x+3y\le 15$, $x\ge 0$, $y\ge 0$.
questions.model:
Draw the lines $x+y=9$ (through $(9,0)$, $(0,9)$) and $x+3y=15$ (through $(15,0)$, $(0,5)$). The feasible region is the bounded region $OABC$ on the origin side of both lines in the first quadrant.
Intersection of $x+y=9$ and $x+3y=15$: $2y=6 \Rightarrow y=3, x=6$.
Corner points and values of $Z$:
Corner point$Z=2x+5y$
$O(0,0)$0
$A(9,0)$18
$B(6,3)$27
$C(0,5)$25
Maximum value of $Z$ is 27 at $x=6, y=3$.

points.t: Correct graph and bounded feasible region

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation $R$ is defined on the set $\mathbb{Z}$ of integers as $R=\{(a,b): 2a+3b \text{ is divisible by } 5\}$. Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation. Also write the equivalence class $[0]$.
questions.model:
Reflexive: For any $a\in\mathbb{Z}$, $2a+3a=5a$ is divisible by 5, so $(a,a)\in R$.
Symmetric: Let $(a,b)\in R$, so $2a+3b=5k$ for some $k\in\mathbb{Z}$. Then $2b+3a=5(a+b)-(2a+3b)=5(a+b-k)$, which is divisible by 5. So $(b,a)\in R$.
Transitive: Let $(a,b)\in R$ and $(b,c)\in R$: $2a+3b=5k$, $2b+3c=5m$. Adding, $2a+5b+3c=5(k+m)$, so $2a+3c=5(k+m-b)$, divisible by 5. So $(a,c)\in R$.
Hence $R$ is an equivalence relation.
Class [0]: $[0]=\{b\in\mathbb{Z}: 3b \text{ is divisible by } 5\}=\{b: b \text{ is a multiple of } 5\}=\{\ldots,-10,-5,0,5,10,\ldots\}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Using integration, find the area of the region bounded by the parabola $y=x^{2}$ and the line $y=2x+3$.
questions.model:
Sketch: the upward parabola $y=x^{2}$ with vertex at the origin and the line $y=2x+3$ cutting it at two points; the region lies above the parabola and below the line.
Points of intersection: $x^{2}=2x+3 \Rightarrow x^{2}-2x-3=0 \Rightarrow x=-1, 3$, i.e. $(-1,1)$ and $(3,9)$.
Area $=\int_{-1}^{3}\left[(2x+3)-x^{2}\right]dx$
$=\left[x^{2}+3x-\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{3}=(9+9-9)-\left(1-3+\frac{1}{3}\right)=9+\frac{5}{3}$
$=\frac{32}{3}$ sq. units

points.t: Correct sketch showing the region between the line and the parabola

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
An online shop sends its parcels through three courier partners X, Y and Z, which handle 50%, 30% and 20% of the parcels respectively. From past records, 2%, 3% and 5% of the parcels handled by X, Y and Z respectively are delivered late.
(i) Find the probability that a parcel chosen at random is delivered late.
(ii) A parcel is found to have been delivered late. Find the probability that it was handled by courier partner Y.
questions.model:
Let $E_1, E_2, E_3$: parcel handled by X, Y, Z; $L$: parcel delivered late. $E_1, E_2, E_3$ form a partition of the sample space.
$P(E_1)=0.5$, $P(E_2)=0.3$, $P(E_3)=0.2$; $P(L|E_1)=0.02$, $P(L|E_2)=0.03$, $P(L|E_3)=0.05$
(i) By the theorem of total probability:
$P(L)=0.5(0.02)+0.3(0.03)+0.2(0.05)=0.010+0.009+0.010=0.029$
(ii) By Bayes' theorem:
$P(E_2|L)=\frac{P(E_2)P(L|E_2)}{P(L)}=\frac{0.009}{0.029}=\frac{9}{29}$

points.t: Events defined with $P(E_1)=0.5, P(E_2)=0.3, P(E_3)=0.2$ and the conditional probabilities $0.02, 0.03, 0.05$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Two drones are flying in straight lines during a light show. With respect to a fixed origin on the ground, their paths are along the lines
$L_1: \vec{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+6\hat{k})$
$L_2: \vec{r}=(-3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+12\hat{k})+\mu(6\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k})$
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Find the direction cosines of the line $L_1$.
(ii) Show that the paths $L_1$ and $L_2$ are perpendicular to each other.

points.t: Dot product of direction vectors $=12+6-18=0$, hence perpendicular

parts.q: (iii) Show that the paths $L_1$ and $L_2$ intersect and find the point at which they meet.
parts.model:
A general point on $L_1$: $(1+2\lambda, 2+3\lambda, 3+6\lambda)$; on $L_2$: $(-3+6\mu, 3+2\mu, 12-3\mu)$.
Equating: $1+2\lambda=-3+6\mu$ and $2+3\lambda=3+2\mu$, i.e. $\lambda-3\mu=-2$ and $3\lambda-2\mu=1$.
Solving: $\mu=1$, $\lambda=1$.
Check in the third coordinate: $3+6(1)=9$ and $12-3(1)=9$. Equal, so the lines intersect.
Point of intersection: $(3, 5, 9)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A farmer has 200 m of fencing wire. He wants to enclose a rectangular field that lies along a straight river bank. No fencing is needed along the river. Let $x$ metres be the length of each of the two sides perpendicular to the river.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Express the area $A$ of the field as a function of $x$.
parts.model: Side parallel to the river $=200-2x$ m. $A(x)=x(200-2x)=200x-2x^{2}$

parts.q: (ii) Find the value of $x$ for which $A'(x)=0$.
(iii) Using the second derivative test, show that the area is maximum at this value of $x$ and find the maximum area.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A welfare group bought rice, wheat flour and pulses for three community kitchens. Let the prices be Rs $x$ per kg of rice, Rs $y$ per kg of wheat flour and Rs $z$ per kg of pulses.
Kitchen 1: 1 kg rice, 1 kg flour and 1 kg pulses cost Rs 170.
Kitchen 2: 2 kg rice, 1 kg flour and 3 kg pulses cost Rs 410.
Kitchen 3: 1 kg rice, 2 kg flour and 1 kg pulses cost Rs 200.
Based on the given information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Write the system of equations in the matrix form $AX=B$ and find $|A|$ and $\operatorname{adj}A$.
(ii) Using $A^{-1}$, find the price per kg of each item.
parts.model:
$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 & -2\\ -1 & 0 & 1\\ -3 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$
$X=A^{-1}B$: $x=850-410-400=40$, $y=-170+0+200=30$, $z=-510+410+200=100$
Rice Rs 40 per kg, wheat flour Rs 30 per kg, pulses Rs 100 per kg.
